Michael —

Putting a short assessment together; quick summary below and attaching a worked runbook + SOC2 snapshot. I'll follow up with an internal ops note to clarify ownership.

Summary (brief):
- Private (VPC / customer-managed): best for strict data egress controls, simpler legal posture for certain regulators, typical procurement + on-prem validation 8–12 weeks. Initial GPU footprint for a 100k monthly active users pilot (safe concurrency) ~ 8x A100 equivalent (can be a mix with quantized instances).
- Dedicated (reserved Redwood pools): faster onboarding (2–3 weeks), predictable latency SLOs and easier burst capacity, lower upfront procurement friction. Footprint for same pilot: ~6x A100-equivalent due to shared KV caching and packing optimizations.

Key differences to call out:
1) Time-to-production: Dedicated wins (2–3 weeks) vs Private (8–12 weeks) for full hardened deployment.
2) Cost profile: Private has higher one-time set-up (network, KMS/HSM integration, audit validation) and slightly higher steady-state unit cost; Dedicated offers better unit economics at scale if you commit.
3) Compliance artifacts: We provide SOC2 + audit logs for both, but Private lets you retain full control of keys and network egress.
4) Support & runbook: For Private we offer an ops-handover + optional managed on-call. For Dedicated, Redwood retains platform ops with escalation paths into customer success + SRE.

I'll loop in Karthik and Marissa for the sizing and procurement timeline details below.

Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
VP, Sales — Regulated Accounts
Redwood Inference

Subject: RE: Compliant deployment — initial ask and timeline

Quick internal breakout with concrete sizing and ops notes. Copying only the internal thread for planning — Michael will get a cleaned summary.

Assumptions (pilot):
- Query profile: 80% short/chat prompts (<256 tokens), 20% long gen (avg 800 tokens)
- Peak concurrent active sessions: 60 (sustained peaks 2–3 minutes)
- Target p50 latency: <250ms for short paths, <750ms for long gen

Sizing estimates (A100-equivalent slots):
- Dedicated (reserved): baseline 6 slots + 2 burst slots (total 8)
- Private (VPC / air-gapped): baseline 8 slots + 3 reserve for redundancy (total 11)

Procurement & timeline notes:
- Dedicated: legal/PO + SOC2 review (if needed) = 2–3 weeks. No HSM required unless customer insists.
- Private: network onboarding (VPC peering / on-prem package), KMS integration (customer HSM) and validation = 8–12 weeks. Plan for an on-site validation window if air-gapped.

Operational responsibilities:
- Dedicated: Redwood provides runtime SRE (patching, kernel selection), customer owns application-level fallbacks. Redwood on-call for platform incidents; escalation to customer via named CS engineer.
- Private: Customer ops owns hardware and network; Redwood provides control-plane support and a managed handover (optional managed-oncall add-on).

Attachments: I've added a sample slot-utilization chart in the runbook.

Karthik
Director, Deployment Engineering

Attached is a concise comparison slide and the sizing runbook. Short answers to your asks:
